passage:
Gargi: manager just gave you the Kolkata account as well?
Harish: yep. third new account this quarter 😅
Harish: everyone else "has a lot on"
Gargi: you have three accounts and Nikhil has one
Harish: I know. but she said "you are the only one I trust with this"
Harish: and I hate that it makes me feel taller
Gargi: ok that's honest
Harish: I do feel used. also kind of proud. both at once
Gargi: want me to come with you when you tell her it's too much?
Harish: maybe. let me think first

qa.q: How many accounts does Harish have compared with Nikhil?
qa.a: Harish has three accounts and Nikhil has one.

qa.q: What mixed feelings does Harish describe about being trusted with the Kolkata account?
qa.a: Harish feels used and also proud at the same time; being trusted feels flattering even though the workload is unfair.

qa.q: What choice does Gargi offer Harish, and why might it help?
qa.a: Gargi offers to come along when Harish tells the manager it is too much, which gives support so that Harish does not have to make the case alone.

qa.q: What might the manager be thinking when handing Harish a third account?
qa.a: The manager probably thinks Harish will always deliver and may not see the total load; the sentence "the only one I trust" suggests relying on reliability without noticing the cost.

grounding: A dependable worker is given extra work because they will always deliver, feeling used but also proud of being needed.

passage: In a small-town post office, Ishita balanced the day's accounts by four, as usual. The postmaster handed her the pension registers as well. "You never make mistakes, Ishita." Deepak, at the next counter, had been on his phone for an hour and was allowed to leave early. Ishita stacked the registers, her jaw tight. She felt used, and yet she stood a little straighter, because the postmaster trusted her. On the way home she rehearsed a sentence to say tomorrow, then dropped it, thinking, they will manage nothing without me.

qa.q: What extra work did the postmaster hand to Ishita?
qa.a: The postmaster handed Ishita the pension registers as well.

qa.q: What mixed feelings does Ishita have while stacking the registers?
qa.a: Ishita feels used, with a tight jaw, and also proud, standing a little straighter at being trusted; the two feelings sit side by side.

qa.q: What could Ishita say tomorrow to keep the trust but reduce the load?
qa.a: Ishita could name what she already handles, show the hours involved, and ask the postmaster to share the pension registers with Deepak.

qa.q: How might Deepak see the afternoon, leaving early while Ishita stays?
qa.a: Deepak may not have thought about the extra load on Ishita at all, or may see leaving early as an easy break; nothing in the scene shows Deepak noticing.

grounding: A dependable worker is given extra work because they will always deliver while others coast, feeling used but also proud of being needed.

passage:
At half past six on Friday, the Kolkata ad agency was emptying. Jyoti waved from the lift. “Weekend, finally!” Two others followed her, laughing.
Mr Ghosh stopped at Seema's desk with a folder. “The tea brand pitch moved to Monday. I need someone who won't let me down.” He smiled. “That's always you, Seema.”
Seema's weekend plans, her cousin's engagement, flashed in her mind. She took the folder anyway.
Alone under the office lights, she felt her jaw tighten. Why is it never Jyoti? she thought. And yet, some small part of her glowed. He trusts me. Nobody else could do this.
She worked till eleven, annoyed and oddly proud at the same time.

qa.q: What time was it when the office was emptying?
qa.a: It was half past six on Friday.

qa.q: What mix of feelings did Seema have working alone?
qa.a: She felt used and resentful that it was never Jyoti, but also oddly proud that her boss trusted only her.

qa.q: What could Seema say next time she's handed extra work?
qa.a: She could say calmly that she has plans and ask whether the work can be shared with Jyoti or another colleague.

qa.q: How might Mr Ghosh see his habit of giving Seema extra work?
qa.a: He probably sees it as a compliment and an easy fix, not noticing it overloads her while others coast.

grounding: Shows a dependable worker given extra work because she always delivers, feeling used but also proud of being needed.

passage:
“Baljeet, the audit files are due Wednesday,” said Sharmila, his manager. “Can you take them? You're the only one who gets them right.”
“I'm already doing the tax returns and Manoj's reconciliations.”
“Manoj is... Manoj,” Sharmila laughed. “You know how it is.”
Manoj, at the next desk, was watching cricket highlights. He didn't look up.
“Fine,” said Baljeet.
At lunch his friend Neeraj asked, “Why do you keep saying yes?”
Baljeet stirred his dal. “Because she asks me. Because I'm good at it.” He paused. “And because it makes me feel I matter here. But also like a donkey.”
Neeraj laughed. Baljeet didn't.

qa.q: What was Manoj watching at his desk?
qa.a: He was watching cricket highlights.

qa.q: How did Baljeet feel about always saying yes?
qa.a: He felt both proud to be needed and used, like a donkey, which left him torn and unhappy.

qa.q: What could Baljeet ask Sharmila for?
qa.a: He could ask for his workload to be reviewed and for Manoj's reconciliations to go back to Manoj, before accepting the audit files.

qa.q: How might Neeraj see Baljeet's situation?
qa.a: Neeraj sees the unfairness clearly from outside and seems puzzled why Baljeet keeps agreeing.

grounding: Shows a dependable colleague given extra work because he always delivers while another coasts, feeling proud and used at once.

passage:
I'm Pooja, and by my third year at the school I had become the teacher who said yes.
Annual day? Pooja will do it. Exam papers for three sections? Pooja. When a colleague went on leave, Aparna ma'am, our principal, gave me her classes too. “You never disappoint me,” she said. Others in the staffroom drank their tea and talked about weekend trips.
I remember walking home one evening with a bag of fifty answer sheets, furious. Why me? Why always me?
And yet, I also remember the warmth when Aparna ma'am thanked me at assembly. Being needed felt good. That was the trap.
It took me a whole year to say, “Ma'am, I can't take this one.” She was surprised, and then she gave it to someone else.

qa.q: How many answer sheets was Pooja carrying home?
qa.a: Pooja was carrying fifty answer sheets.

qa.q: What mixed feelings did Pooja have about being the one who said yes?
qa.a: Pooja felt furious and used, but also warm and proud at being needed and thanked, which made the pattern hard to break.

qa.q: What finally changed things, and why did it work?
qa.a: Saying "Ma'am, I can't take this one" showed the principal the limit, and the work was simply given to someone else.

qa.q: How might Aparna ma'am have seen Pooja before that day?
qa.a: She likely saw Pooja as endlessly reliable and didn't realise how overloaded Pooja was.

grounding: A teacher recalls being given extra work for always delivering while others coasted, feeling used and proud at once.

passage:
Supervisor's note, claims team, end of quarter.
I've been part of the problem. Every time something urgent came in this quarter, I gave it to Minakshi, because she always delivers. The clinic audit, the backlog from Swati's leave, the Friday reports: Minakshi. Meanwhile Swati and Rohit left at five most days with half their queues untouched, and nobody asked why.
This week I noticed Minakshi eating lunch at her desk three days running. When I thanked her in the team meeting, she smiled and said, "Happy to help." Later, in the lift, she said quietly, "Sometimes being good at this feels like a punishment." Then she laughed and added that she does like being the one people count on.
What I did next: I moved the Friday reports to Rohit, asked Swati to take back her own backlog, and set time to ask Minakshi what she'd like to hand over, not just what she can carry.

qa.q: Where did Minakshi eat lunch three days running?
qa.a: At her desk.

qa.q: What mixed feelings does Minakshi show in the lift?
qa.a: She feels used and worn out, as if being good at the job is a punishment, yet also proud of being the one people count on.

qa.q: Why might the supervisor's changes help Minakshi?
qa.a: Spreading the work back to Swati and Rohit and asking what Minakshi wants to hand over stops her reliability being turned into extra load.

qa.q: How might Rohit react to suddenly getting the Friday reports?
qa.a: Rohit may be surprised or a bit annoyed at first, but it also shows that the uneven effort has finally been noticed.

grounding: Shows a dependable colleague who keeps getting extra work while others coast, feeling both used and proud of being relied on.
